title: Every message into an agent is tracked by its id: the text Spawn types carries a marker, and the commands API and the agent page say each message recorded, typed, taken, answered, not taken within its bound, or taken twice; a message not taken is an alert in Needs you
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (`type_once`: the one place the Bridge stages the text of a command into an engine, after its workspace notices; `step` and the `cmd_<id>:typing` and `cmd_<id>:typed` records; `SessionView::typing` and `answered`: an input waits until the one before it was answered, so two inputs never land in one prompt; `type_prompt` for a start or resume with a prompt), crates/spawn-core/src/ingest.rs (`user_turn` and `claude_line`: a transcript's user line is `message.received`, keyed by the line's uuid, with no detail; `turn_duration` and an interrupt are `turn.stopped`, an API error `turn.failed`) and crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs (`EventKind`; `notice.typed` and `notice.received` are the read-only precedent of a typed thing and its arrival), crates/spawn-core/src/transcripts.rs (`read_from_transcript`); crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (`SESSION_COMMANDS`, which `GET /api/fleet/<session>/commands` answers through serve.rs's fleet views, and `UNTOLD_MERGES` for how a `typed` step is read) and crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_events`, `spawn_commands`, `spawn_now_ms`, `spawn_alert_record`); crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the module comment: an alert fires once per occurrence, rests on records or a reading, and is never fired twice whatever restarts; `Monitor::start` reads `known` back; `commands` and `command_failed`; `a_restart_keeps_main_red_one_alert`); web/src/commands.ts, web/src/components/fleet/AgentDetail.tsx (the agent page's commands) and web/src/home.ts (an open alert reaches Needs you); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3.4 (Alerts).

The problem. What Spawn types into an agent (a person's input, the dispatcher's task, a send-back, a digest, a supervisor's nudge) is a command, and the records say when it was created and when its text was typed, and separately that a prompt reached the engine (`message.received`), with no id. So nobody can say which message an engine took, whether it took one twice, whether the turn it started ended, or that one was never taken: an input typed into a pane that dropped it, or one the Bridge could never type, looks like any other finished or pending command, and the owner learns of it when a worker sits idle. GitHub #41 asks for one id per message, carried end to end, and a lifecycle read from records.

Required behaviour.
(a) The marker. The text the Bridge types for a command carries the command's id in a marker the engine's transcript keeps, `[spawn message #<command id>]` (its own line, after the text; the notices before it are part of the same message). Every command whose text is typed carries it: an input, and a start or resume with a prompt. A transcript user line (not a tool result) that holds a marker is that message taken: one `message.taken` record naming the command (detail `command_id`), keyed by the line and the id, so a line re-read after any restart records nothing again; a line with two markers takes both. The `message.received` it is stays as it is.
(b) The lifecycle, from records only. `GET /api/fleet/<session>/commands` gives each command a `message`, null for a command that types nothing (a key, a stop, a start with no prompt): `{state, typed_at_ms, taken_at_ms, answered_at_ms, taken, not_taken}`. `typed_at_ms` the Bridge's `typed` step; `taken_at_ms` the first `message.taken` naming it, `taken` how many name it (2 when the engine wrote its line twice); `answered_at_ms` the first `turn.stopped` or `turn.failed` of the session after its first `message.taken`. `state` is `answered`, else `taken`, else `typed`, else `recorded`. The same text sent twice is two messages, each read by its own id, never by text or order. Times are the records' (`recorded_at_ms`), on the database's clock.
(c) Not taken. `not_taken` is true while a message has no `message.taken` and was recorded SPAWN_MESSAGE_TAKEN_SECS (default 120; whole seconds, a bad value warned once and the default used) ago or more: typed and never taken, or never typed. A command recorded before this change carries no marker and is never `not_taken` (how you tell is yours; say it in the docs).
(d) The alert. The alerts step raises `message_not_taken`, subject the session, key `message_not_taken:<command id>`, evidence the command, agent, session and whether it was typed, once per message when it becomes `not_taken`; it clears when the message is taken, or when the session ends with it untaken. An open one reaches /api/alerts and Home's Needs you, which names the agent and the message. A restart of the loop fires none again and loses none (read back from the store; a test through a restart, like `a_restart_keeps_main_red_one_alert`, and one that the start reads it back).
(e) The page. web/src/messages.ts exports `messageLine(command)`, the words for a command's message: null for none; "not typed yet", "typed, not taken yet"; once `not_taken`: "not taken (never typed)", "not taken (typed)"; once taken: "taken in <d>" (from the command's creation), then " · answered in <d>" (from the taking) once answered, then " · taken <n>×" when taken more than once. <d> is "<1 s", "<n> s" under a minute, "<n> min" under an hour, "<n> h", rounded down. messages.ts and its imports load with node alone (relative imports with the .ts extension, `import type` for types, no packages, erasable TypeScript only). The agent page shows each command's line beside it.
(f) Nothing else changes: the order the Bridge types in, the wait between inputs, what a refused or unknown typing does, `message.received`, and every other alert stay as they are. docs/fleet-architecture.md says the marker, the lifecycle, the bound and the alert.

Out of scope (objective 046): an explicit acknowledgement by the agent (`spawn ack <id> done|declined`) and an `acted` state; reading a reply's content; retrying a message that was not taken.

Checked by rsi/scenarios/045.sh: a real `spawn loop` and `spawn serve` with four workers on a fake engine: one takes each message (its task, then two inputs with the same text, each tracked by its id to answered), one never takes what is typed (typed, `not_taken` after the bound, one alert), one whose pane refuses the paste (recorded, never typed, one alert; typed, taken and answered once it takes a paste, its alert cleared), one that writes each prompt twice (taken 2); then the loop and serve restart: every message reads as before, no alert fires again, and a new input is tracked; and messages.ts's words under node.
